app.title: Lemmata — Multilingual Topic Modeling
app.summary: A person uploads text files or pastes text, previews them, and sets the language, chunk size, number of topics, part-of-speech filter and custom stopwords in the sidebar before running the analysis. The interface lemmatises and filters the texts, fits an LDA model and reports coherence and model metrics. It can also sweep topic counts to suggest how many topics to use. The person then opens each topic's words and its most representative document, renames topics, and looks at how topics spread across documents in a heatmap, stacked distribution, trend view and topic map. They can check exactly what preprocessing kept or removed, then download a ZIP of CSV/JSON results, chart images and an environment record, or a PDF report.

task.text: Discover the topics in a text corpus with a reproducible LDA model, interpret and name them, and export the matrices and a report.

data.text: A corpus of plain-text, PDF, Word, ODT or EPUB documents in one language. A single file is split into word-count chunks at sentence boundaries; several files each become one document. The model produces a document-term matrix, topic word weights and a document-topic matrix.
data.item: a document or chunk of a text, and the topics fitted across them

stage.text: exploring a text corpus with topic modelling, after the texts are collected and before interpretation and write-up

mechanism.text: Sidebar parameters and a disabled-until-upload Run button drive a pipeline whose results appear in seven tabs. Topic labels edited in the sidebar carry through to every chart and export. A topic selector opens one topic's bars or word cloud, word weights and its highest-weighted document.

field.text: LDA topic modelling of literary and historical texts in the digital humanities

workflow.name: fit an unsupervised model to a document collection, interpret and name its components, and export them

steps.here: Multi-file uploader for txt/pdf/docx/odt/epub, or a paste box. A preview shows each file's size, word count and first 200 characters, and warns about duplicate content or very uneven file sizes.

steps.step: set the computation's parameters before running it
steps.here: Sidebar settings: language, chunk size, number of topics, words per topic, a POS preset or custom tags, and custom stopwords. Under Advanced: seed, max iterations and min_df/max_df. It shows an estimated run time and warns when there are too many topics for the documents. Run Analysis stays disabled until there is text.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: The pipeline lemmatises, builds the document-term matrix, fits LDA and scores C_v coherence. Overview shows coherence colour-coded with a suggestion, plus perplexity, log-likelihood, vocabulary kept and removed, and top lemmas. A coherence sweep over k=2–15 suggests the best topic count.

steps.step: open one item in detail and name it
steps.here: Select a topic to see its top words as a bar chart or word cloud, a rank/word/weight table and the excerpt from its highest-weighted document. The sidebar editor renames topics, and the names carry through to every chart and export.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: A document × topic heatmap with hover values, stacked topic-share bars per document, a trend chart of topic weight in document order with file boundaries marked, and a map of topic distances and prevalence.

Counts of original tokens, tokens after stopwords and final lemmas. Also shown: chunks per file with an imbalance note, built-in vs custom stopwords removed, a per-document table, and a token-level table for any chosen document.

A ZIP with topic_words.csv, doc_topic_matrix.csv, preprocessing_summary.csv, metrics and results JSON, charts and environment.json, named by language, topic count and time. Also a PDF report, individual file downloads, and heatmap PNG/SVG.

distinctive: A coherence sweep refits the model across a range of topic counts and names the best-scoring one, so the topic number need not be guessed.
Every word's fate is traceable: a token-level table shows the original form, lemma and whether it was kept or removed, and stopword removal is split into built-in and custom.
Results are made reproducible on purpose: a fixed seed and batch learning, with an environment record of package versions and parameters in every export.
One uploaded file is chunked at sentence boundaries while several files stay whole documents, and the topic count is capped at half the number of documents.

Linguistic filtering is done before modelling: a spaCy model for the chosen language lemmatises the text and keeps only the selected parts of speech, and a warning appears when the text does not seem to match the chosen language.
